Q: Why does Python allow out-of-range slice indexes for sequences? A:

The documentation has your answer:

s[i:j]: slice of s from i to j (note (4))

(4) The slice of s from i to j is defined as the sequence of items with index k such that i <= k < j. If i or j is greater than len(s), use len(s). If i is omitted or None, use 0. If j is omitted or None, use len(s). If i is greater than or equal to j, the slice is empty.

The documentation of IndexError confirms this behavior:

exception IndexError

Raised when a sequence subscript is out of range. (Slice indices are silently truncated to fall in the allowed range; if an index is not an integer, TypeError is raised.)

Essentially, if len(p) < 20 stuff like p[20:100] is being reduced to p[len(p):len(p)]. p[len(p):len(p)] is an empty slice at the end of the list, and assigning a list to it will modify the end of the list to contain said list. Thus, it works like appending/extending the original list.

This behavior is the same as what happens when you assign a list to an empty slice anywhere in the original list. For example:

In [1]: p = [1, 2, 3, 4]

In [2]: p[2:2] = [42, 42, 42]

In [3]: p
Out[3]: [1, 2, 42, 42, 42, 3, 4]

Q: Architecture for handling OAuth token refresh across multiple services in agent-based systems A:

Yes , the usual production pattern is not to let every worker refresh independently when they share the same delegated user credential. If multiple workers can refresh the same OAuth refresh token, you can get race conditions, that es more clear with refresh-token rotation. The safer approach is a centralized token manager (or shared store with per-credential locking / single-flight refresh): workers call getValidToken(...), and only one refresh runs for a given credential while the others wait or reuse the updated token. For client_credentials jobs with no user context, replicas can usually fetch tokens independently. In practice, the split that works best is: frontend refresh synchronized locally, backend machine tokens fetched independently, shared user tokens refreshed centrally/serially.

Q: How to exclude 0 from MIN formula Excel A:

A nice solution without an array formula, if you only want to ignore the zeroes, is to find the Xth smallest value after the zeroes:

=SMALL(A1:E1,countif(A1:E1,0)+1)

Q: Does Amazon S3 support HTTP request with basic authentication A:

Off-topic.
It seems like the best approach is to create your own intermediate server to access objects from the client's application.

For example, let's say you have infrastructure with a few services:
1. messenger app
2. project manager app(jira-like)
3. any other app

And your services have the common IAM provider.

And you want to be able to:
1. share your S3 objects between these apps;
2. immediate revoke/grant permissions for a specific object for any user;

I think the best decision is to create intermediate(let's say USER_S3_OBJECT_GETTER) server with only 2 HTTP endpoints:
1. HTTP GET
2. HTTP OPTIONS(for CORS)

When a user in messenger app will UPLOAD a file via messenger backend's API - messenger will put the object into S3. But you will return the URL to the USER_S3_OBJECT_GETTER server.
When this user will try to get this file - it will go to USER_S3_OBJECT_GETTER server and provide its auth data in any allowed way(JWT, JWE, Bearer header, etc..). And permissions for the file will be checked at the very time the user is trying to get it.
